analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date, a new drain paragraph (head lines ~926-932) and a status-output paragraph on enabled_models restart diffs (head ~998-1013). I examined both supplied head-text units against the threat model; the unchanged logout and revoke text in the same file was read for context only. There is no source, config, or protocol change here, so no control is altered.

The drain paragraph describes behavior with the coordinator connection down. A drain with no unfinished work waits up to 10 seconds and then finishes without an acknowledgement. The text justifies this because the disconnect already cancelled accepted work and nothing queued can still reach the coordinator. The paragraph also says shutdown waits 15 seconds per model unload, and that a model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit. Both are availability and lifecycle statements (T-010, T-029 area). The claim that the disconnect cancels accepted work depends on the provider implementation (ServiceDrain.swift, ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown) and on the coordinator-side drain barrier. Neither is in the supplied evidence.

One residual question for integration: if a stalled model unload is left to process exit, GPU-resident plaintext KV or prompt data (T-028) remains until the process exits. Process exit also relies on the stop flow, which does not depend on this unload. This is a doc-described behavior, not a demonstrated regression.

The status paragraph is operator-facing diagnostics about enabled_models drift. It exposes no secrets or identifiers beyond the local operator's own view.

T-053 (stale authorization) and A-008 (token revocation) are unchanged. The logout text still says only HTTP 204 confirms remote revocation. No threat-model update is needed from this PR.
